newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK July industrial production data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK July industrial production data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing July industrial production up 0.5 percent m/m, 0.9 percent y/y and manufacturing output up 0.5 percent and 0.3 percent respectively:
Market expectations were 0.5 percent m/m and 0.8 percent y/y for industrial production and 0.3 and 0.1 percent for manufacturing output.
"At last it seems to be coming into line with the surveys we've had recently. Slightly higher than the market consensus."
"It's a good number. I'd expect this modestly positive tone to continue in the months ahead."

"UK manufacturing output rose a stronger than expected 0.5 percent in July. Coming on top of a smaller revised fall in June, the data should be seen as consistent with the apparent decision to leave rates on hold this week. The report also supports the view that much of the stock overhang problem has now been addressed. If so, the bullish picture of consumer spending painted in the new CBI survey should be equally optimistic for output prospects. Fits in with the widely held scenario that growth will accelerate through the remainder of 1996.""

"These are the first signs of an upturn in manufacturing but there is clearly still a long way to go. It is also clear that manufacturers are still able to meet what is undoubtedly an upturn in demand out of stocks. The real pickup in output is a story for next year, not this."
